newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. bond vol hit, traders liquidate puts.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. bond vol hit, traders liquidate puts.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond volatilities were crushed as the underlying futures rallied sharply Tuesday on a smaller than expected gain in the first-quarter employment cost index.

In the wake of the 0730 CDT (1230 GMT) data, implied volatility for June bond options sank a full point from opening levels, collapsing to 8.80 percent. It had crept back up to 8.95 percent by day's end, versus about 9.40 percent late Monday.
September bond volatility was quoted at 9.10 percent late in the session, down from 9.40 percent Monday.
Floor traders in both Treasury bonds and Eurodollars said heavy liquidation of put positions accompanied the data-inspired rally in futures.
"That number we got today has to make you change your thinking," said one bond options trader who began the day bearish.
By relaxing fears of spiraling wage inflation, the employment cost index opened the door for the Fed to leave rates unchanged at the May policy meeting, he said.

The 0.6 percent rise in the first-quarter employment cost index was below average forecasts for a 0.9 percent gain. The government this morning also released bullish data on durable goods sales, which declined a steep 3.0 percent in March.
Late in the session, some sizable call purchases also surfaced in bond options,, with two Wall Street dealer firms picking up a total of 3,000 in the June 109-00 strike.
June bond futures settled at 108-30, up 1-17/32 on the day, and September Eurodollars gained 18 basis points to end at 93.875.
The bond trader predicted June volatility would push back above 9.00 percent by week's end, approaching the April jobs report Friday, then quickly drop two points after the number.

Several additional key indicators are due out before Friday, beginning with the preliminary first-quarter U.S. gross domestic product report on Wednesday, which should underpin interest rate volatilities, traders said. Next week, however, economic news will be sparse.
Economists in a Reuters survey on average estimated GDP grew by 4.1 percent in the first quarter.
The Chicago purchasing managers survey will also be released Wednesday, followed by the national purchasers survey and March personal income and consumption data on Thursday.

In Eurodollar options, volatility was steady at 11.20 percent in September and 12.60 percent in December. A floor analyst attributed the lack of movement to futures' return to a familiar price area in pulling away from the bottom of the recent trading range.
